items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Oscar and I had more in common... Oscar and I thought alike... Whe he'd come to town he would kind of seek me out, or if I was around him I would seek him out. And we would play

ctx.x: Who was the first one to establish the guitar in jazz?

In jazz, well I think that Eddy Durham in my opinion was one of the early ones. And then came Charlie Christian. And there is a guitarist that we just haven't mentioned at all, and I think that in his way -- he was as great as Charlie, but in a different way. Oscar Moore. Oscar Moore was a great guitarist. I had the utmost admiration for

Oscar Moore. But unfortunately -- not unfortunately, but at that time there was just two styles, and Charlie Christian had a more exciting style. Charlie played like a horn, you know. He was a driving guitarist, amazing technique and all this. But musically, when we come down to musically that Oscar Moore was -- he was just something else.
